description:
pkix-ct/src/sct.rs:56-83

`SignedCertificateTimestamp` is `pub struct` with seven public fields and
no `#[non_exhaustive]`. Once 0.0.0 ships, the maintainer cannot:

- Add a new field (no `#[non_exhaustive]`, so callers can use struct
  literal `SignedCertificateTimestamp { ... }` exhaustively).
- Change `signature: Vec<u8>` to a typed signature enum once
  RustCrypto's `signature` crate stabilizes a parsed form.
- Change `extensions: Vec<u8>` to a typed `Vec<CtExtension>` after
  RFC 6962bis defines extension types.
- Make `version` private (callers already match on it directly).

The wire-form fields belong in a sealed type with accessor methods, or
the struct should be `#[non_exhaustive]` so callers cannot use struct
literals against it.

Recommendation: add `#[non_exhaustive]` to all wire-form structs in
this crate's public surface (`SignedCertificateTimestamp`, `CtLog`,
`SignedTreeHead`, `MerkleAuditPath`). Per non-negotiable #6 these
types must remain `Clone+Debug+PartialEq+Eq+Hash` and serde-able, but
that does not require exhaustive struct-literal construction. Provide
a `new()` or `builder()` constructor and document direct field access
as the only way to construct.

Caller impact when un-fixed: every 0.x release that adds a single
field is a major bump. Adoption-blocker for downstream crates that
pin to `^0.1` and expect 0.x minor compatibility.
title: SignedCertificateTimestamp lacks #[non_exhaustive] — all fields public, breaking changes locked
